body:
Exact bounded result for **cycle-three**, with a companion calculation for [mixed-biweight](https://github.com/hodge-computer/sextics/discussions/56): **neither fixed target admits a certificate with denominator degree at most five.** Complex coefficients, the complete numerator space, and nonzero quotients are included. Degrees six and higher remain open; neither instance is solved.

Prepared with OpenAI Codex assistance for `rbajaj5`, including separate construction and review agents. Both threads were read before this calculation; they contained no research comments. The protected targets and existing upstream files remain unchanged from `b8c4edeb80a82395ec07164caf445cfa43bbbd56`, also unchanged at current main `0768616c9b70b318011b7c421abdd640322ccbfc`.

**Complete first-equation calculation.** Let $J=(\partial_iF)$, $q=1$, and $A=X_0^3Y_0^3$, as specified in both records. Euler normalization makes every certificate satisfy $N(F)=AD$. We compute the entire map

$$
S_d\longrightarrow S_{d+6}/J_{d+6},\qquad D\longmapsto[AD].
$$

Both instances have the following exact ranks. The numerator map includes all six components of degree $d+1$; no denominator shape or extra symmetry is imposed.

| Degree $d$ | Denominator coefficients | Numerator-map rank | Augmented rank | Denominator kernel |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 0 | 1 | 36 | 37 | 0 |
| 1 | 6 | 126 | 132 | 0 |
| 2 | 21 | 336 | 357 | 0 |
| 3 | 56 | 756 | 812 | 0 |
| 4 | 126 | 1497 | 1623 | 0 |
| 5 | 252 | 2682 | 2928 | 6 |

**The degree-five kernel fails a necessary second equation.** It is exactly the gradient span:

$$
D=a\cdot\nabla F,\qquad N=Aa+K.
$$

All 90 linear multiples of the 15 Koszul fields are checked to be independent and exhaust the numerator kernel, whose dimension is $2772-2682=90$. Every component of $K$ belongs to $J$. Writing $B_D(N)=D\operatorname{div}N-N(D)$, we have $D\in J$, $F\in J$, and

$$
B_D(Aa+K)\equiv-A\cdot a^{\mathsf T}\operatorname{Hess}(F)a\pmod J.
$$

Thus every certificate must annihilate the 21-column quadratic map in $S_{10}/J_{10}$, with the factor two on off-diagonal Hessian columns. Its exact rank is **21 for each instance**: the Jacobian image has rank 1497, and the augmented rank is 1518. Six exported rational functionals annihilate $J_{10}$ and isolate the six squares $a_i^2$. Consequently every $a_i=0$, contradicting $D\ne0$.

**Reproduce and inspect.** [Immutable argument, proof packets, two actual-map figures, checks, and bounded-attempt logs](https://github.com/rbajaj5/hodge-lab/blob/02026b32f13ec54bf115ec5cbe1814796cacd2ad/notes/fresh-instance-baselines.md). From that Hodge Lab checkout, initialize its pinned submodule and run:

```sh
python3 -S experiments/fresh_instance_e1.py verify
```

This requires only the Python standard library. The rational check covers 1,845,216 E1 Jacobian pairings, 12 numerator lifts, and 18,144 E2 Jacobian pairings; 26 altered records/functionals are rejected. A separate implementation reconstructs the targets, checks ranks modulo 1009 with matching characteristic-zero upper bounds, and independently verifies all 12 rational square functionals. Canonical LF bindings and an isolated LF-file replay address Windows checkout differences. Local checks pass; remote CI is not being claimed here.

This is a lower degree bound, not an existence certificate, a Lean theorem, or a solve submission. Degree six is unattempted. Passing the Jacobian quotient test would only be necessary, not sufficient.

Credit: the repository authors' certificate framework and Euler normalization, its complete Jacobian/Koszul formulation in Chapters 1 and 5, the bridge attributed there to Benjamin E. Diamond, and Griffiths's residue theory. These computations use that framework; no quantum-group or p-adic theorem is assumed.
